A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, LLMs on the Line: Data Determines Loss-to-Loss Scaling Laws. All 29 pages, including Appendices A–H, equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training and evaluation results across over 6000 checkpoints, including intervention experiments, Table 1's model comparisons, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original training, evaluation, and intervention results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The scaling-law fitting procedure in Section 3 and Appendix B, model configurations, and intervention procedure in Section 4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining corpora, including FineWeb-Edu, C4, and Pile variants, and the same validation datasets and nine downstream tasks. Appendix coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator groups in Figures 4–6, Mamba–Llama comparisons in Table 1, and pretrained model inventory in Table 3 are identical. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 5000-sequence validation sampling, downstream loss evaluation, tokenizer comparisons using bits per byte, training budgets, model sizes, and optimization settings.

E4.justification: The interventions on data, tokenizer, architecture, size, context length, and optimization are unchanged. Appendices D–H retain the same curve-area analysis, alternative x-axis comparisons, individual-dataset analyses, and additional train-to-test plots.

E5.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same statements about collecting checkpoints across sizes and seeds. Goodness-of-fit reporting is unchanged, with no added uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains average test losses of 3.88 for Mamba and 4.04 for Llama in the larger FineWeb-Edu pair, and Table 4 retains the base-versus-data curve area of 0.22.

T1.justification: Equation (1)'s shifted power law and Equations (2)–(5)'s compute-to-loss relationships and irreducible-error definitions are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: pretraining data primarily determines loss-to-loss scaling, while architecture and other training choices generally have limited influence.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning architectural biases, possible effects of weight tying, and data curation are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same qualifications about intervention coverage, alternative training paradigms, and fitting with intermediate checkpoints.

D1.justification: Implementation frameworks, tokenizers, hyperparameters, model specifications, fitting instructions, and resource-access information are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment supplies no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to prior loss-to-loss scaling and robustness studies. The additional acknowledgment is funding attribution, not a research citation.

P1.justification: v3 adds acknowledgment of BMFTR funding under grant 01IS24085C (OPENHAFM), changes appendix references from 'App.' to the section symbol, and updates the arXiv stamp. The scientific prose and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The added acknowledgment causes limited reference reflow on page 10, and reference-formatting edits produce small typographic changes elsewhere. All 34 figures and four tables retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds funding attribution and makes small formatting changes, but preserves the scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations throughout the main text and appendices. These administrative and typographic edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
